discord.safety.does: What this app does for you
discord.safety.does_1: It sends nothing on its own. Every message, reaction and click needs your key or click, with the window in front.
discord.safety.does_10: It never downloads member lists or whole histories. It loads only what you open and scroll to.
discord.safety.does_11: It opens invite links in your browser. Joining servers is done in Discord itself.
discord.safety.does_12: It sends no friend requests and changes nothing in your profile.
discord.safety.does_13: It reconnects slowly and resumes your session instead of logging in again; a connection that keeps dropping waits a few minutes.
discord.safety.does_15: When Discord pushes back (a captcha, a verification, "too fast"), it goes quiet for a while and tells you what to do; the third time in a day, for the rest of the day.
discord.safety.does_16: A new account, or one with no verified email, gets lower limits and no new DMs for its first 7 days.
discord.safety.does_17: It never shows or solves a captcha. Do that step in the official app.
discord.safety.does_18: It keeps your token in this computer's keychain and forgets it when you log out.
discord.safety.does_2: It never retries a failed message by itself. Press it again to resend.
discord.safety.does_3: It slows you down when you go faster than a person: you see "Slow down: wait N s." and a countdown.
discord.safety.does_4: It keeps a day's total of messages, reactions, edits and deletes, and stops at a busy person's day.
discord.safety.does_5: It refuses the same message twice in ten minutes, in any channel or DM.
discord.safety.does_6: It refuses more than 5 mentions (@everyone, @here and roles count), 3 links or 1 invite in one message, and @everyone where you may not use it.
discord.safety.does_7: It opens new DMs only with friends and people who share a server with you, and pauses when you write to many people you had not talked to in a while.
discord.safety.does_8: In a server you joined a moment ago, links and mentions wait 10 minutes.
discord.safety.does_9: It follows each channel's slowmode and your permissions, and tells you before Discord refuses.
discord.safety.honest: Honestly: Discord's terms forbid unauthorised software and automated access, and the authors of other third-party clients say plainly that using one is against them. They also report that Discord rarely acts on the client itself, but on behaviour that looks like a bot, and that third-party clients trip its spam filter more easily. This app does not pretend to be the official one. Use it at your own risk.
discord.safety.intro: This app talks to Discord as you, with your account. Discord does not approve third-party apps, and its rules forbid bots that run a person's account. It acts on accounts that behave like bots or spammers. This app keeps you to a person's pace; the rest is up to you.
discord.safety.not_verified: not verified (verify it in the official app)
discord.safety.safe_mode_hint: Only what you do yourself goes out: no typing indicator, read marks, presence, GIFs, pins or older pages.
discord.safety.should_1: Try this app on a secondary account first, or on one you could afford to lose.
discord.safety.should_2: Verify your email and add a phone number in the official Discord app.
discord.safety.should_4: Never give your token or password to anyone. If it may have leaked, change your password.
discord.safety.should_5: Turn off your VPN or proxy when you log in.
discord.safety.should_6: Use the official app or discord.com for joining servers, friends, your profile and security settings.
discord.safety.should_7: Do not stay logged in with the same account on many computers at once.
discord.safety.should_8: Do not use macros or scripts with this app.
discord.safety.should_9: If Discord warns you, stop, and check User Settings, Account Standing in the official app.
